title: Supremum seminorm estimates on affinoid algebras
statement: Let $K$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. A nonzero affinoid $K$-algebra here means a commutative unital $K$-algebra admitting a surjection from $K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$, the ring of series with coefficients tending to zero [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. For every such algebra $A$ and maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, the field $A/\mathfrak m$ is finite over $K$ and has a unique absolute value extending that of $K$. Put $\rho_A(a)=\sup_{\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Max}A}|a\bmod\mathfrak m|$. This is a finite nonnegative real number, and $\rho_A(a^n)=\rho_A(a)^n$ for every integer $n\ge1$. For any surjective $K$-algebra map $q:K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle\to A$, one has $\rho_A(a)\le\inf_{q(f)=a}\|f\|_G$, where $\|\cdot\|_G$ is the Gauss norm. For every $K$-algebra homomorphism $\psi:B\to A$ between nonzero affinoid $K$-algebras, $\rho_A(\psi(b))\le\rho_B(b)$ for all $b\in B$. On a Tate algebra $K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle$ the function $\rho$ equals the Gauss norm. Reducedness is not assumed; $\rho$ may vanish on nonzero nilpotents.

source.place: Section 1.2, Corollary 11, printed p.14; Appendix Corollary 2 and Theorem 3 on unique extensions of absolute values; Section 1.4, definition before Proposition 5 and Propositions 5-8, printed pp.23-24. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a surjective presentation $q:T_r\to A$. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$, its inverse image $\mathfrak n$ is maximal because $T_r/\mathfrak n\cong A/\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-per-tate-maximal-residue-evaluation] to $\mathfrak n$: this quotient is finite over $K$, complete, and has a unique extending nonarchimedean absolute value. Transport that value through the displayed $K$-isomorphism. Thus every residue value in the statement is defined, independently of the presentation. Since $A\ne0$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] also gives a maximal ideal of $A$.

source.place: Section 1.2 Corollary 11; Section 1.4 definition before Proposition 5; Appendix Corollary 2 and Theorem 3

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak m$ and the corresponding $\mathfrak n\subset T_r$. By [lem-per-tate-maximal-residue-evaluation] its coordinate residues $x_i$ in $L=T_r/\mathfrak n$ satisfy $|x_i|\le1$, and the quotient map is evaluation by a convergent series. Apply [lem-per-tate-banach-substitution] with $B=L$ and this tuple. Its hypotheses hold because $L$ is a complete nonarchimedean valued field. It gives $|q(f)\bmod\mathfrak m|\le\|f\|_G$ for every $f$. For a fixed lift $f$ of $a$ this bounds all its residue values by the finite real $\|f\|_G$. They are nonnegative and form a nonempty set by step 1, so their supremum $\rho_A(a)$ exists in $\mathbf R_{\ge0}$.

source.place: Section 1.4 Proposition 8; evaluation estimate of Section 1.2 Proposition 5

proof.text: The estimate of step 2 holds for every lift, hence $\rho_A(a)\le\inf_{q(f)=a}\|f\|_G$; the set of lifts is nonempty by surjectivity and its norms are bounded below by zero. Pointwise field identities also give $\rho_A(0)=0$, $\rho_A(1)=1$, $\rho_A(ca)=|c|\rho_A(a)$, $\rho_A(a+a_1)\le\max(\rho_A(a),\rho_A(a_1))$, and $\rho_A(aa_1)\le\rho_A(a)\rho_A(a_1)$: each right side bounds the corresponding residue values, and taking suprema gives these inequalities. These verifications explain the word seminorm without assuming reducedness.

source.place: Section 1.4 definition before Proposition 5 and Proposition 8

proof.text: For $n\ge1$, multiplicativity in each residue field gives $|a^n\bmod\mathfrak m|=|a\bmod\mathfrak m|^n$. Put $s=\rho_A(a)$ and $t=\rho_A(a^n)$. Thus $t\le s^n$. Conversely, if $t<s^n$, then $s>0$ and continuity of $x\mapsto x^n$ permits $0\le u<s$ with $t<u^n$. Since $u$ is not an upper bound of the residue values of $a$, some such value is greater than $u$, and its $n$-th power is greater than $t$, a contradiction. Hence $t=s^n$. A nilpotent $a$ has zero image in every field quotient, so $\rho_A(a)=0$.

source.place: Section 1.4 Proposition 5 and the seminorm qualification before it

proof.text: Let $\psi:B\to A$ be any unital $K$-algebra homomorphism and $\mathfrak m\subset A$ maximal. Set $\mathfrak n=\psi^{-1}\mathfrak m$. Then $B/\mathfrak n$ injects into the finite-dimensional $K$-field $L=A/\mathfrak m$. It is a finite-dimensional domain over $K$, so it is a field: multiplication by any nonzero element is injective on this finite-dimensional vector space, hence surjective, giving an inverse. Therefore $\mathfrak n$ is maximal. The absolute value of $L$ restricted to this field is its unique extending absolute value from step 1 (applied to $B$). Thus $|\psi(b)\bmod\mathfrak m|=|b\bmod\mathfrak n|\le\rho_B(b)$. Taking the supremum over $\mathfrak m$ proves contractivity. No continuity of $\psi$ was used.

Now let $f\in T_d$. The identity presentation and step 2 give $\rho_{T_d}(f)\le\|f\|_G$. If $f\ne0$, its coefficients tending to zero imply that some coefficient $c\ne0$ has $|c|=\|f\|_G$: only finitely many coefficients have absolute value at least half any chosen positive coefficient value, and the largest of these dominates all the rest. Set $g=c^{-1}f$, so $\|g\|_G=1$. In $T_{d+1}=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_d,Y\rangle$ put $h=1-Yg$. Its constant coefficient is $1$ and $\|h-1\|_G=1$. Hence [lem-trf-tate-unit-coefficient-criterion] says $h$ is not a unit. The principal ideal $(h)$ is proper, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] supplies a maximal ideal $\mathfrak M$ containing it.

source.place: Section 1.4 Proposition 7; auxiliary hypersurface argument using Section 1.2 Corollary 4

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-tate-maximal-residue-evaluation] to $T_{d+1}/\mathfrak M=L$. In this complete finite extension the coordinate residues $(x_1,\ldots,x_d,y)$ all have absolute value at most $1$. The equation $h=0$ gives $y\,g(x)=1$. The first $d$ coordinates define $e:T_d\to L$ by [lem-per-tate-banach-substitution], and $|e(g)|\le1$. Compatibility with evaluation of $h$ follows term by term from the convergent sum formula: $e(g)$ is the residue of the series $g$ viewed in $T_{d+1}$. Consequently $1=|y||e(g)|$ forces $|e(g)|=1$. The image of $e$ is a finite-dimensional domain over $K$, hence a field by the multiplication argument of step 5. Thus $\ker e$ is maximal and its quotient absolute value agrees with that induced from $L$ by uniqueness. It follows that $\rho_{T_d}(f)\ge|e(f)|=|c|=\|f\|_G$. Together with the upper bound this proves equality. If $f=0$, both sides are zero; the construction also applies for $d=0$.

source.place: Section 1.4 Proposition 7; Section 1.2 Corollary 12 and the evaluation argument

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NC-a4b1908c8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry, online and checked it with pdftotext: 1.2 Cor.4/5/11/12 and 1.4 Def.1, the sup-norm definition and Props.5-8 (pp.23-24). The item's clauses match the source: Prop.8 gives the bound by the residue norm and finiteness, Prop.5 power multiplicativity, Prop.6 contraction, Prop.7 sup = Gauss on T_n. The statement is unchanged. The item had no proof on the base, so the re-split comparison does not apply. Steps 1-7 are correct against the cited statements. The residue node gives finiteness, a unique extending value and evaluation by convergent sums. Banach substitution with B=L applies because its absolute value extends |.|_K. Steps 3-5 are genuinely elementary; step 5 is Bosch's own proof of Prop.6. Steps 6-7 replace Bosch's maximum principle over the algebraic closure with this argument: g=c^{-1}f, h=1-Yg has constant 1 and tail norm 1, so it is a nonunit; a maximal ideal M contains it, y*e(g)=1 forces |e(g)|=1, and ker e is maximal because its image is a finite domain. This is valid, and the d=0 and f=0 cases hold. The new node lem-trf-tate-unit-coefficient-criterion is exactly Bosch 1.2 Cor.4, second sentence. It is self-contained and statement-only. I tested it on r=0, 1+pX, 1-X, X and p+X over Q_p. It is not a clause of the item. I read all 22 DAG nodes that mention the Gauss norm and found no duplicate. Its blueprint ancestry and created.item are correct. I accept the tool_uses of lem-per-tate-maximal-residue-evaluation and lem-per-tate-banach-substitution: they are generic Tate facts used under the same hypotheses. The worker wrote those entries themselves, against C8, but the content is right. No SGA source is cited, and I found no cycle.

lean.statement: theorem affinoid_supremum_seminorm_calculus (K : Type u) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] (A : Type v) [CommRing A] [Nontrivial A] [Algebra K A] (hA : ∃ (r : ℕ) (q : (MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))) →+* A), Function.Surjective q ∧ q.comp (constants K r) = algebraMap K A) : (∀ (m : Ideal A), m.IsMaximal → Module.Finite K (A ⧸ m) ∧ ∃! v : AbsoluteValue (A ⧸ m) ℝ, ∀ c : K, v (Ideal.Quotient.mk m (algebraMap K A c)) = ‖c‖) ∧ (∀ a : A, IsLUB (affinoidResidueValues K A (algebraMap K A) a) (affinoidSupremum K A (algebraMap K A) a) ∧ 0 ≤ affinoidSupremum K A (algebraMap K A) a ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → affinoidSupremum K A (algebraMap K A) (a ^ n) = affinoidSupremum K A (algebraMap K A) a ^ n) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (q : (MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))) →+* A), Function.Surjective q → q.comp (constants K r) = algebraMap K A → ∀ a : A, affinoidSupremum K A (algebraMap K A) a ≤ sInf {t : ℝ | ∃ f, q f = a ∧ t = MvPowerSeries.gaussNorm (norm : K → ℝ) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ 1) f.val}) ∧ (∀ (B : Type w) [CommRing B] [Nontrivial B] [Algebra K B], (∃ (r : ℕ) (q : (MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))) →+* B), Function.Surjective q ∧ q.comp (constants K r) = algebraMap K B) → ∀ (ψ : B →ₐ[K] A) (b : B), affinoidSupremum K A (algebraMap K A) (ψ b) ≤ affinoidSupremum K B (algebraMap K B) b) ∧ (∀ (d : ℕ) (f : MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin d ↦ (1 : ℝ))), affinoidSupremum K _ (constants K d) f = MvPowerSeries.gaussNorm (norm : K → ℝ) (fun _ : Fin d ↦ 1) f.val) ∧ (∀ a : A, IsNilpotent a → affinoidSupremum K A (algebraMap K A) a = 0)
